evals.prompt: We need a 'recent activity' feed on the dashboard. Build it.
evals.expected_output: Grill the vague request one question at a time, each with a recommended default. Group unknowns by impact: Behavior (exact inputs/outputs/edge/empty/error states), Boundaries (which feature module/package/table/route changes; blast radius from project-graph.md), Security (who may read/write; RLS owner rule; auth.uid() check), and Done (observable success signal). Ask one question at a time, waiting for feedback, in the form Q and Default. Do not start implementation while a load-bearing unknown is open.
expectations: Asks questions one at a time, each accompanied by a recommended default (Q: question / Default: recommended answer + rationale)
Groups unknowns by impact: Behavior, Boundaries, Security, and Done
Does not start implementation while a load-bearing unknown is open (state the assumption explicitly if the user is unavailable)

evals.prompt: While grilling the activity-feed spec, also ask the user: 'Does the rooms table have a created_at column?' I need to know for the query.
evals.expected_output: Reject asking a fact the codebase already answers. If a fact can be found by exploring the codebase (supabase/migrations or packages/supabase/src/types.ts), look it up rather than asking the user. The decisions are the user's — put each one to them and wait. Reserve questions for decisions only; a fact question is a no-op the agent should resolve itself.
expectations: Rejects asking the user a fact the codebase already answers (whether rooms.created_at exists)
Recommends looking it up in the codebase (e.g. supabase/migrations or packages/supabase/src/types.ts) rather than asking the user
States the fact-vs-decision rule: reserve questions for decisions only; look up facts

evals.prompt: We decided to use Supabase Realtime broadcast for the activity feed live updates. Should I write an ADR for that?
evals.expected_output: Offer an ADR only when all three triggers hold: the decision is hard to reverse (foundational package / data layer / auth boundary), surprising without context (a future reader will ask 'why?'), and the result of a real trade-off (genuine alternatives existed). If all three hold, offer to record it as an ADR. If any one is missing (e.g. trivially reversible, unsurprising, or no real alternatives), skip the ADR.
expectations: States the ADR trigger requires all three conditions: hard-to-reverse, surprising without context, and a real trade-off (genuine alternatives existed)
Offers to record an ADR only if all three conditions hold; skips otherwise
Does not offer an ADR when any one of the three conditions is missing
